reference: Achiever LayersView.xaml EyeVisibilityButtonStyle: smooth almond outline and centered iris ring, consulted only as a visual reference.
prompt: Use case: logo-brand. Create a perfectly clean minimal desktop UI icon: one flat pure white eye on a perfectly uniform solid black background. A smooth horizontal almond outline, with a single centered circular iris outline, transparent-looking black holes. Symmetric and exactly centered in a square canvas. No grain, no transparency, no alpha texture, no gradients, no speckles, no glow, no shadows, no text. Smooth rounded consistent strokes about 1/18 of eye width. Almond outline has two graceful continuous arcs, width approximately twice its height. Iris ring diameter a little over half the eye height, separated from eyelid by black space. White shape occupies 82 percent of canvas width. This is a precise binary white-on-black stencil/mask for a small layer visibility button, inspired by Achiever's simple curved outline eye. Just the two white outlines on pure black.
refinement_prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Refine this generated white-on-black eye stencil for a tiny desktop visibility button. Preserve its smooth almond contour, exact symmetry, centered circular iris and overall dimensions. Increase the thickness of BOTH white outlines to approximately DOUBLE their current thickness, using a consistent medium-bold weight so the eye reads clearly at 18 pixels wide. Preserve black separation between iris and eyelid and a generously open black iris center. Pure flat solid white strokes, perfectly uniform solid black background. No transparency, no grain, no shadows, no glow, no highlights, no text or extra shapes. Center the eye exactly on the square canvas.
preparation: Convert the generated white-on-black stencil luminance to alpha (values <= 8 become transparent, >= 247 opaque, linear in between). Center its visible bounds in a 64 x 64 canvas, with a 56-pixel visible width, preserving aspect ratio. Use white RGB pixels for palette tinting. Save the identical RGBA8 pixels as layer-eye.png and layer-eye.rgba.
